intended_object: The n-th exterior power ⋀^n_R M of an R-module M over a commutative ring R, seen as an object of the category of R-modules. Taken from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition wraps Mathlib's `exteriorPower R n M` (notation `⋀[R]^n M`) as an object of `ModuleCat R`, using `↧`. Mathlib's `exteriorPower R n M` is the submodule of the exterior algebra spanned by products of n vectors. This is the standard n-th exterior power, and it is canonically isomorphic to the quotient of the n-th tensor power. It is the right object even when n = 0 (it gives R) and when M = 0.

The universe level `max u v` is forced, because the exterior algebra lives in a universe that depends on both R and M.

The commutative-ring assumption is the setting in which exterior powers are standardly defined, and it is the setting of Mathlib's own `ExteriorAlgebra`. So the definition is at its natural generality: it is simply the categorical version of the linear-algebra construction.
